name: Sunsama
summary: Daily planning that pulls tasks from your other tools into one deliberate schedule.
best_for: people whose problem is deciding what to do today rather than tracking what exists — it pulls from your existing tools and forces a daily plan, which is the whole product
skip_if: you already plan your day and just want a task list, because that is free everywhere; also skip it for a team, since there is no team pricing and the per-person cost multiplies straight through
honest_knock: The pricing page contradicts itself: the plan card says $17 yearly and $22 monthly, the FAQ on the same page says $20 yearly and $25 monthly. One of those is stale, and until you know which, treat $25 as the number you might actually be charged. That is an odd thing to have to say about a company that goes out of its way on that same page to explain why it refuses to use $24.99 pricing — the transparency is real and so is the inconsistency. The other thing to be clear about is that this is per person with no team discount mentioned: two people is two subscriptions, and their own example says $50.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month billed yearly, $22 monthly on the plan card
pricing.notes: (2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit) The page gives two different numbers and it is worth knowing both. The plan card says $17 a month billed yearly, or $22 billed monthly, for the Pro plan, with unlimited usage and integrations; Enterprise is quote-only. The FAQ on the same page says Sunsama costs $25 a month per person, or $20 a month on yearly plans, and gives a worked example of $50 a month for two people. There is a free trial with no card required. The page also explains, unprompted, that they price at $25.00 rather than $24.99 because they consider the latter 'deceitful psychological trickery'. Their own llms.txt, read the same day, lists Pro at $17 per person a month billed yearly and $22 billed monthly, plus a 14-day trial at $0 with no card required — so the machine-readable file agrees with the plan card and not with the FAQ.

compare_with.name: Motion or Akiflow
compare_with.why: the direct daily-planning peers — all three are per person, so compare on which one actually gets you to close the planning ritual each morning
